name: Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome, Encephalomyopathic Form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset progressive encephalopathy with muscle weakness and hypotonia
Demonstration of significant mitochondrial DNA depletion in affected tissues (muscle or liver biopsy)
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes involved in mtDNA maintenance (e.g., TK2, SUCLA2, SUCLG1)
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid
MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy or basal ganglia abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early onset encephalopathy with muscle involvement plus either mtDNA depletion confirmed in tissue or pathogenic nuclear gene variants identified
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, genetic, and histopathological data.

searchTerms: severe loss of movement and mental skills
significant regression in motor and cognitive abilities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked mitochondrial DNA depletion in muscle tissue
searchTerms: marked mitochondrial DNA loss in muscle
very low mitochondrial DNA in muscle tissue
severe mitochondrial DNA shortage in muscle

occasional.notes: May manifest as elevated liver enzymes

imaging: MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Basal ganglia signal abnormalities on MRI
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TK2, SUCLA2, SUCLG1, or other nuclear genes involved in mtDNA maintenance
Confirmed mitochondrial DNA depletion in muscle or liver biopsy
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase deficiency

distinguishingFeatures: Onset typically in infancy or early childhood with refractory seizures
Characteristic symmetric lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem on MRI
Multiple genetic causes including mitochondrial and nuclear DNA mutations

redFlags: Marked lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
references: El-Hattab AW, Scaglia F. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes: review and updates of genetic basis, manifestations, and therapeutic options. Neurotherapeutics. 2013;10(2):186-198.
Spinazzola A, Zeviani M. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2016.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, encephalomyopathic form. ORPHA:254803.
commonPitfalls: Frequently misattributed to primary muscular dystrophies due to prominent myopathy.
May be mistaken for Leigh syndrome because of overlapping neurologic features and lactic acidosis.
Liver involvement can be under-recognized, leading to missed diagnosis in patients with hepatic dysfunction.
Symptoms may be attributed to static encephalopathy, missing the progressive nature of the disease.

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Absence of POLG mutations and presence of severe myopathy with mitochondrial DNA depletion on muscle biopsy favors MDS encephalomyopathic form.
MDS encephalomyopathic form typically shows marked reduction in mitochondrial DNA copy number in muscle, which is not a feature of classic Leigh syndrome.
MDS encephalomyopathic form presents with multisystem involvement (neurologic, hepatic, myopathic) and lactic acidosis, unlike isolated muscular dystrophies.

ruleOutCriteria: Normal mitochondrial DNA copy number in affected tissues (e.g., muscle biopsy) essentially excludes the diagnosis.
Identification of an alternative genetic diagnosis fully explaining the phenotype (e.g., confirmed POLG-related Alpers disease).
